complaints.problem: Correct answers are repeatedly the longest, most specific options and often mirror chapter vocabulary, while distractors rely on obvious overreach or out-of-frame moves.
Sarah, Mathieu, and Ingrid recur across unrelated scenarios in different roles, which can make the case set feel unintentionally continuous.
The title and core-skill line repeat the same phrase, creating a mild scaffold/template smell.

parsedReview.oneParagraphVerdict: The chapter teaches one clean move well: sort facts, feelings, and identity before choosing words. It is memorable, beginner-friendly, practical, and unusually honest about limits. I would not ship it as-is against a professional assessment bar because the quiz pattern is too easy to game without reading; the prose can carry the lesson, but the quiz needs tighter, less telegraphed distractors.
